findings.body: The standard requires “TypeScript in strict mode.” The new hooks have no TypeScript configuration or strict compiler check. This invocation runs them using Node's type stripping, which performs no type checking and ignores tsconfig files ([Node documentation](https://nodejs.org/api/typescript.html#type-stripping)). The repository test command at forge.toml:6 likewise runs only pytest. Add strict type checking against Claude Code's declarations to the required checks; executing the hooks successfully does not enforce this standard.
findings.title: Standard: TypeScript in strict mode

findings.body: The improved between-refresh elapsed assertion, unknown worker start case and stage-outcome assertions exist in core.test.ts, but the repository suite never invokes this file. forge.toml:6 runs pytest, and test_mod_plugin.py imports the production hooks through its Node harness instead. Consequently, the supplied green close run does not exercise these new regression assertions. SHIP owns the native plugin test job (plans/FORGE-MOD-1.md:243), so ensure that task runs core.test.ts with `claude plugin test` and propagates failures. This is deferred advice because the Tasks table assigns that execution check to SHIP.
findings.title: Later: SHIP must run the native CORE regression tests
